It affects axios versions 0.28.0 through 1.17.x; version 1.18.0 is the first patched release. Attackers can supply FormData with field names containing thousands of nested bracket segments (e.g., a[x][x]...) to exhaust the JavaScript call stack and trigger a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded, causing request failure or process termination. The vulnerability was published on August 1, 2026, and carries a CVSS v4.0 base score of 6.3 (Medium) (GitHub Advisory, GitHub Advisory DB). Técnicas The root cause is uncontrolled recursion (CWE-674) leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400) in lib/helpers/formDataToJSON.js. The function parsePropPath() converts a FormData field name like a[x][x][x] into path segments, and the nested buildPath(path, value, target, index) function recursively calls itself once per path segment without enforcing any maximum depth limit. By contrast, the inverse serializer lib/helpers/toFormData.js already implements a maxDepth guard (defaulting to 100) that throws an AxiosError with code ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED — no equivalent protection exists in formDataToJSON. The vulnerable path is triggered when: (1) axios.formToJSON() or the named formToJSON export is called directly with attacker-controlled FormData, or (2) FormData is sent via axios with Content-Type: application/json, which invokes the default transformRequest. A proof-of-concept is publicly available in the official security advisory (GitHub Advisory). Impacto Successful exploitation results in a Denial of Service against server-side applications that process untrusted FormData field names through axios's FormData-to-JSON conversion. In the default axios request path, the RangeError is produced before any network I/O and surfaces as a rejected Promise; in applications that do not handle the rejected promise or catch the synchronous exception from direct formToJSON() calls, the Node.js process may terminate entirely. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact — the vulnerability is limited to availability of the affected application (GitHub Advisory, GitHub Advisory DB).
